messages.text: IN MY END IS MY BEGINNING

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's article page and its grid picture, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Divine female cases

parts.note: thecae are cases or sheaths in botany and anatomy, plural of theca

explanation.surface: A goddess is said to be the one hearing legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle the definition-only clues define two words: the second word's first letter moves to the second-last place to make the first. That is the motto's beginning ending up at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft and crossroads, a divinity who is female.

clue.text: Country yokel's girl not quite accepting ring

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shortened word holds the next piece within it
something not quite complete stops short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin's girlfriend hasn't quite agreed to wear an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS cut to LAS takes O inside. 'yokel's' gives Y, starting the down half of the message, MY BEGINNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, so it is a country.

clue.text: County bowler determined to go at end of season reportedly

indicators.note: this places one piece after the other, so the earlier word ends the answer

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the spoken sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a season of the year, spelt here to match the county's opening
set means resolved or fixed on a course

explanation.surface: A county cricket bowler has resolved to retire as the summer closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county with a cricket side, which suits the bowler. 'bowler' gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England, so it names a county directly.

clue.text: Employment made dreary — somehow one is pleasantly distracted

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in another order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Work that has become dull leaves someone gazing happily out of the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment' gives E. The definition reads as 'one who is pleasantly distracted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer is a person lost in pleasant fantasies rather than attending to the task in hand.

clue.text: Noisy celebration around busy centre — glasses are being drunk

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
c is circa, Latin for around, used before dates

indicators.note: a drink is taken in, so the little word is swallowed inside the larger one

parts.note: a hive is a centre of busy activity
taken as written

explanation.surface: At a rowdy party in a lively town centre, glasses are being drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glasses' gives G. A chivaree is the American spelling of charivari, a mock serenade with pots and pans for newlyweds.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari or chivaree is a raucous mock serenade, a noisy kind of celebration.

clue.text: Mad Irene phoned, interrupting performance

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is something performed, an act
rang is the past tense of ring, to phone

explanation.surface: An angry Irene rang up and broke into the middle of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irene' gives I, the first letter of the across half of the message, IN MY END IS M.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged is a synonym for insane, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Weeping bird

parts.note: an egret is a white heron

explanation.surface: A bird is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Greet is Scots for weep, and also a noun for weeping. The bird's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish and northern dialect, greet means to cry, and a greet is a bout of crying.

clue.text: Jet descended finally — that hurt intolerant ears initially

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
what one cries when something hurts

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter of that word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A plane's jet roared as it landed, painful to sensitive ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aircraft, but it is a jet of water. 'intolerant' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A douche is a jet of water directed at the body, so a jet is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Plant poet

parts.note: Horace was a Roman lyric poet

explanation.surface: A spy has been planted as a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: Orache is a leafy herb of the goosefoot family, eaten like spinach, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Guy and girl playing duet — nostalgic gentleness

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: a piece being played is performed in its own way, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
taken as written
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A couple play a wistful duet together, softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nostalgic' gives N. Mansuetude is an archaic word, from Latin mansuetus, tame.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansuetude means meekness or mildness of temper, a literary synonym of gentleness.

clue.text: Seedy joint very much in decline

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word that follows it

parts.note: to die away is to decline
V is the abbreviation for very
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A run-down bar is badly on the slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' gives M. Die is a verb here: to fade away or decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a disreputable bar or club, a seedy place of entertainment.

clue.text: Yorkshire Post editor taken aback by boy or girl in 18

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two parts stand next to each other

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: something taken aback is pushed backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: ED is the standard short form of editor

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word for the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: the answer to 18 down, abbreviated as it is in school names
Pat is a name used by both men and women

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is shocked by a pupil's behaviour at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire Post' is a real newspaper, but 'Yorkshire' is the extra word giving Y, and Post alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To post a letter is to send it off, which is what despatch means as a verb.

clue.text: Roguish squire paced endlessly around neighbourhood

indicators.note: moved around means shifted about, so the letters are put into a new order
without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before it is cut
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A shifty country gentleman kept walking round and round the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neighbourhood' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Picaresque describes fiction about a likeable rogue's adventures, so it means involving roguery.

clue.text: Rough old weapon

parts.note: asper is Latin for rough, as in the Greek rough breathing, spiritus asper

explanation.surface: A crude, antique weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here. The Greek h-sound mark is called the asper.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pointed weapon used since ancient times, so it is an old one.

clue.text: Baptist's food? Conservative American Evangelist tucked into portion

indicators.note: what is tucked into something is pushed inside it

parts.note: one's lot is one's portion or share
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
US for American
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A traditionalist American preacher digs into a plate of the Baptist's diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evangelist' gives E. John the Baptist lived in the desert on locusts and wild honey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospels say John the Baptist ate locusts, so the insect is fairly called his food.

clue.text: Drink fellow has a right to swallow — nice rest for worker sitting down

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so the fellow holds the next piece

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow
A plus R, the abbreviation for right
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to a drink and a nice sit-down after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' gives N. 'rest' is a support, not a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapboard is a flat board laid across the knees as a desk or work surface for someone seated.

clue.text: Biologically change upsetting mushrooms — I had indigestion

indicators.note: upsetting turns something upside down, which in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: ceps are edible boletus mushrooms
taken as written
had a meal, ate
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: Eating some mushrooms upset my stomach and changed me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indigestion' gives I. The surface invites reading 'had indigestion' together, but 'had' alone gives the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To speciate is to form new species in the course of evolution, a biological change.

clue.text: Snooker den that is occupied by male nerds

indicators.note: a place occupied by someone has them inside it

parts.note: a sty is a filthy den
i.e. stands for id est, that is
M is the abbreviation for male
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A snooker hall is a den full of geeky blokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nerds' gives N. Snooker is a verb here: to block or thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, just as snookering someone leaves them blocked.

clue.text: Educate second naughty child, John needing bringing up

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
CH is the abbreviation for child

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue goes from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, and loo is the British word for one
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: Teaching a second unruly child, John needs better upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' gives N. 'John' looks like a boy's name; here it is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or teach them, a verb synonym of educate.

clue.text: Analyse excuse

parts.note: spare me, excuse me from it

explanation.surface: Pick apart a pretext.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to analyse it into its grammatical parts.

clue.text: Downpour disturbed water-averse pet, an animal getting caught in it

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: in it says the letter sits inside the word just named

parts.note: cats famously dislike getting wet
the indefinite article
a rat is an animal
c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cloudburst upset the water-hating cat, and some creature got caught in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' gives D and looks like the anagram signal. Nothing is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract can mean a great torrent of rain or water, a deluge.

clue.text: Brown mammal

parts.note: a stoat is a small mammal of the weasel family

explanation.surface: A brown-coated animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to brown it under heat, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Pet panics

parts.note: scares are panics or frights

explanation.surface: A pet animal is in a state of alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here. Pet is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to stroke fondly, and a caress is exactly that gentle touch.

clue.text: Little woman's son Eastern idol influenced

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women, and 's is kept
S is the abbreviation for son
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A woman's son has been swayed by an idol from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'influenced' gives I. 'Little woman' reads as a wife, but it is one of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A joss is a Chinese household god or its image, an idol of the East.

clue.text: They have many silly faces — I had a score with contortions

parts.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

indicators.note: contortions twist things out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Clowns pulling silly faces: I scored twenty, contorting my face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' gives S and sits inside the definition, which reads 'They have many faces' without it. A score is twenty, the number of faces on an icosahedron.
explanation.definitionFit: Icosahedra are solids with twenty flat faces, so they have many faces.

clue.text: Bird in coarser grass nesting

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted lie inside the clue's own words, straddling the gap between them

parts.note: the tail end of the word
the opening of the word
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message; it is skipped over

explanation.surface: A bird is nesting in rough grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the extra word 'grass' (giving G) is lifted out, the bird is hidden across 'coarser nesting'.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: Shoot author

parts.note: a sprout is a new shoot on a plant

explanation.surface: An order to fire at a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's first letter moves to second-last place, as in every definition-only clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Head of 18 into fancy modern lit. ain't classics teacher?

indicators.note: into places the single letter inside the rearranged ones
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a different order

parts.note: the letters as written, without the punctuation

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the answer to 18 down
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A headmaster asks whether modern literature is a matter for the classics master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modern' gives M, completing IN MY END IS M across. The question mark flags that a Latinist need not be a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is a scholar of Latin, the sort who might teach classics.
